prepareDescription: Choose the service and check what you need before entering settings.
configureDescription: Use only the resources and permissions this Agent needs. Follow the service settings below to configure its access.
reviewDescription: Name this connection and decide how it is available to Agents. Save only when these settings are right.
advancedHint: Optional tool alias and additional instructions. Most connections can keep the defaults.
name: Connection name
workspaceScope: Workspace shared — attach it to the Agents that need it
secretsOmitted: Credentials are not shown in this summary. Existing credentials stay unchanged unless you replace them.
saveHint: Add or Save stores these settings. A connection test is a separate, explicit action; it does not grant access or save changes.
localSaveHint: Add or Save stores these settings. Runtime access and risk acknowledgement remain governed by the controls above.
testHint: Test results describe that request, not permanent health or every allowed operation. After changing settings, test again when you want to verify them.
oauthNext: For OAuth, first add this Toolkit, then open its settings and choose Connect. Saving alone does not authorize an account.
savedHint: You are editing a saved Toolkit. Replace credentials only when needed; account connection actions can take effect separately from saving settings.
keyIdentity: Service account in the supplied key
storedCredentials: Credentials are saved. Their values are hidden; leave them unchanged to keep using this connection.
analyticsRuntime: This Toolkit runs in the Agent Runtime. Starting an inactive Runtime can take time; connection testing and tool execution are separate actions.

mcp.purpose: Connect tools offered by a remote MCP server.
mcp.prepare: Get the MCP endpoint and supported authentication method from the server owner. Use a trusted server: it will receive the requests sent to its tools.
mcp.configure: Enter the server URL, choose the matching authentication method, and supply credentials only in the credential fields. Advanced endpoints and timeout are optional.
mcp.verify: Run Test Connection explicitly to check the server response or discover OAuth metadata. OAuth discovery does not sign you in.
mcp.recovery: Check the endpoint, network reachability and authentication method. For OAuth, confirm the saved connection is authorized; changing discovery fields does not grant access.

github.purpose: Manage a GitHub connection using its existing account or App identity.
github.prepare: Know whether tools should act as a person or an App installation. Use the existing setup controls for the selected mode.
github.configure: Keep the existing identity unless you intend to replace its registration or credentials. Select only the feature groups and repositories needed.
github.verify: Review the connection evidence returned by GitHub. Runtime token injection is a separate opt-in with its own acknowledgement.
github.recovery: Check token expiry, App settings, installation access and organization approval. Reauthorize through the connection controls; do not paste a secret into the name or description.

google.purpose: Connect Google tasks to the account and access you explicitly approve.
google.prepare: Use a Google account with access to the required files, calendars or mail. Available tasks are provided by the existing Google setup.
google.configure: Choose tasks, authorize the account, then review the actual granted access in the Google setup. Reconnection is separate from editing this connection's name.
google.verify: Use the returned account and access review. Selected tasks alone are not evidence of granted permissions.
google.recovery: If access is partial or expired, review the missing tasks and reconnect. Organization policies may require an administrator's approval.

notion.purpose: Let Agents work with Notion content you authorize.
notion.prepare: Have a Notion account with access to the workspace and content you want to use. This connection uses Notion's OAuth service; no integration token is required here.
notion.configure: Add the Toolkit first. Reopen its settings and choose Connect to authorize Notion. Keep the default timeout unless requests need longer.
notion.verify: After authorization, use the saved connection's Test Connection action. Adding the Toolkit does not by itself give access to Notion content.
notion.recovery: Reconnect if authorization expires. Check the chosen Notion workspace and content access if expected pages are missing.

sentry.purpose: Investigate Sentry issues and enable only the actions you need.
sentry.prepare: Use a Sentry account with access to the intended organizations and projects. Triage and management features can change issue or project state.
sentry.configure: Select the skill groups, add the Toolkit, then reopen settings and Connect to Sentry. Feature selection does not grant Sentry permissions.
sentry.verify: After authorization, test the saved connection. Confirm the account can access the intended projects before asking an Agent to change anything.
sentry.recovery: Check account permissions and project access, then reconnect if required. Reduce selected features if the intended workflow is read-only.

aws.purpose: Use AWS Managed MCP with the AWS permissions you explicitly provide.
aws.prepare: Prepare an access key ID and secret for an IAM identity with only the required downstream AWS service permissions. Choose the region where the work should run.
aws.configure: Enter the key pair in the credential fields. If assuming a role, add its ARN and required external ID; both the caller and role trust policy must allow that assumption.
aws.verify: Use Test Connection to check the supplied or saved credentials. A successful test does not certify permission for every AWS service action.
aws.recovery: Check the key pair, region, IAM policy, role trust and external ID. Do not add broad administrator permissions just to make a test pass.

gcp.purpose: Choose Google Cloud services and the access an Agent may request.
gcp.prepare: Prepare a project ID and a service-account JSON key. Enable the required services and grant the account the roles appropriate to the selected tools.
gcp.configure: Select services, opt into write access only where needed, and paste or upload the key. The role list below describes configuration needs, not permissions already granted.
gcp.verify: Run Test Connection after entering the project and key. The email parsed from a key is input metadata until the provider verifies the request.
gcp.recovery: Check the project ID, JSON key, enabled APIs and IAM roles. If write calls fail, review the specific service permission instead of broadening all access.

google_analytics.purpose: Read Google Analytics reports through a service account.
google_analytics.prepare: Enable the Google Analytics Data and Admin APIs, create a service-account key, and grant that account access to the Analytics property.
google_analytics.configure: Paste or upload the JSON key. Optionally enter a default numeric property ID; leave it empty when you want to select from accessible properties later.
google_analytics.verify: Test the connection after granting property access. A valid Google Cloud key alone does not grant access to an Analytics property.
google_analytics.recovery: Check API enablement, the service-account email in property access management, and the property ID. Account access and Analytics property access are separate.

brave_search.purpose: Search the web with your Brave Search API subscription.
brave_search.prepare: Create an API key in the Brave Search API dashboard and confirm the subscription has quota.
brave_search.configure: Enter the API key and choose country, language and Safe Search defaults. These defaults affect results, not which account is authorized.
brave_search.verify: Test Connection sends an explicit request that may consume quota. It does not save the key or guarantee future quota availability.
brave_search.recovery: Check the key, subscription quota and rate limit. If the key was rotated, use Replace Key and save the new value.

kubernetes.purpose: Give Agents scoped access to selected Kubernetes clusters.
kubernetes.prepare: Prepare a kubeconfig, service-account token, or the supported cloud credentials for each cluster. Ensure the cluster API is reachable from the service.
kubernetes.configure: Choose each cluster's authentication method, then restrict namespaces and resource kinds. Keep read-only mode unless mutations are intended; Secret access is denied by default.
kubernetes.verify: Test the configured cluster access explicitly. UI restrictions are additional controls and do not replace Kubernetes RBAC or cloud IAM.
kubernetes.recovery: Check the API endpoint, certificate, token or cloud identity, and RBAC. Do not disable TLS validation or grant cluster-admin just to bypass an error.

shell.purpose: Review the existing shell network restrictions.
shell.prepare: Determine which domains the Runtime needs to contact. This settings surface does not create or authorize a new Runtime.
shell.configure: Use the existing allow and deny controls. Keep the current defaults unless the intended network access requires a change.
shell.verify: These are configuration rules, not a live connection test or evidence that commands have succeeded.
shell.recovery: Review the exact requested domain and current Runtime policy. Do not relax unrelated restrictions to bypass a denied request.

other.purpose: Configure the service selected from the Workspace catalog.
other.prepare: Follow this provider's documentation and use only the access required for your workflow.
other.configure: Use the available settings below. The server catalog determines which providers can be created.
other.verify: Use a connection test only when the provider offers one. Saving settings does not prove live connectivity.
other.recovery: Review the error and provider requirements. Keep credentials in their designated fields.
